dedupe_keys.name: monitoring the impact of energy conservation measures with artificial neural networks

description: Elissaios Sarmas and colleagues publish this resource through Zenodo. The executed application estimates adjusted baseline energy after renovation of a Latvian educational building. Measures affect heating, ventilation and envelope insulation. Feedforward neural networks use time-of-day, day-of-week and weather features to predict baseline electricity and diesel consumption and are compared with degree-day regression. The source reports greater accuracy for the neural estimates but gives no numeric score in the abstract. This case supports measurement and verification of building-energy conservation measures. It does not equate a predicted baseline with directly measured counterfactual consumption or establish unrestricted access to the building observations. Native metadata gives open access and the licence label cc-by-4.0. These terms describe the deposit; a paper licence does not establish a software licence. Coverage is limited to the stated sites, model settings and application examples. Only descriptive metadata and file descriptors were inspected. Linked data, code and document bodies were not opened.
